notes.meaning: Israel had false prophets alongside the true ones, and the church will have false teachers too. They slip their wrong ideas in quietly, side by side with true teaching, so at first no one notices. A "heresy" here means a self-chosen belief that does not come from God and leads to ruin. These teachers even deny Jesus, the Master who bought them with his blood, and so they bring quick ruin on themselves.

differ.view: Christ bought even these men who end up lost, so he died for all people, not only for those who will be saved.
Some who believe Christ died only for those who will be saved read "Master" as God the Father, who "bought" his people in a more general sense.

notes.meaning: Many people will follow these teachers into their immoral ways. Because these followers call themselves Christians, outsiders will blame the Christian faith itself, "the way of truth," and speak evil of it. This is a call for us to live so that no one has reason to mock the faith.

These teachers are driven by love of money. They use smooth, made-up words and treat people like goods to sell for profit. God settled their judgment long ago. It is not idle or asleep, even if it seems slow. It is on its way.

Peter now gives examples from the past to prove that God will judge. Even angels, the highest of God's creatures, were not spared when they sinned. God threw them into "Tartarus," a Greek word for the darkest place of punishment. There they are held as if in chains of darkness until the final judgment. If God punished them, wicked teachers cannot hope to escape. Scripture says little about how or when the angels fell, so we should not guess.

God did not spare the world before the flood, even though its people were many. Their great numbers did not protect them. But he kept Noah safe with seven others, eight people in all. Noah lived rightly and also warned people for many years to turn back to God, both by his words and by building the ark.

God burned the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah to ashes because of their great sins. They stand as a warning for everyone who would later live without God. God hates the same sins in every age, and he does not judge one people more lightly than another.

God also rescued Lot. Lot is called righteous because the main direction of his life was upright, even in a wicked city. Day after day he saw and heard the lawless deeds around him, and it tormented his soul. He never got used to sin. When others' sins grieve us instead of seeming normal, that helps keep us pure.

Here is the point of the whole list: the Lord knows how to rescue his people from trials, even when they can see no way out. God's people will face trials, but he keeps them through those trials and brings them out. He also keeps the wicked under his control, held for punishment on the day of judgment. Even if their punishment seems delayed, they will not escape.

Judgment falls especially on those who chase sinful bodily desires and look down on authority. These teachers are bold and self-pleasing. They are not afraid to insult "glorious beings." Many older commentators take these to be rulers and leaders whom God has placed in authority.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars suggest the "glorious beings" here are angels rather than human rulers.

notes.meaning: Angels are far stronger than these men, yet they do not bring insulting charges before the Lord. Even when angels report wrongdoing to God, they do it calmly, without abuse. Jude tells how the angel Michael said only, "The Lord rebuke you." If we must complain about wicked people, we should bring it to God with calm and compassion, not rage.

These teachers are like animals without reason, driven by appetite, that seem made only to be caught and killed. They mock things they do not understand. Their own corruption will bring them to ruin, just as a wild animal's nature leads it into the trap.

The harm that comes to them is the fair pay for their wrongdoing. They party openly in broad daylight, without any shame. They are like stains on a clean garment and bring disgrace on the church. They even join the church's shared meals while enjoying their own deceptions.

Their eyes are always looking with lust, and they never stop sinning. Like hunters setting bait, they trap people who are not yet firm in their faith. Their hearts are trained in greed the way an athlete trains for the games. "Accursed children" means they live under God's curse.

They have left the straight path and copied Balaam. Balaam was a prophet in the book of Numbers who loved money and wanted to curse Israel for pay. Later he advised Moab to lead Israel into sexual sin and idol worship. These teachers are like him in their greed and in leading others into sin.

God stopped Balaam in a startling way: his own donkey, which could not talk, spoke with a human voice. A dumb animal stood in the way of a prophet's mad, money-driven plan. Even this wonder did not truly turn Balaam's heart. People who will not listen to ordinary warnings are rarely changed by miracles.

These teachers are like a dry well in the desert, or a cloud blown away before any rain falls. They promise refreshment but give nothing. God's truth is like living water, and they have none of it. Because they spread darkness now, the deepest darkness is kept for them forever.

They use big, impressive-sounding words that are really empty. They bait people with permission to give in to bodily desires. Their targets are new believers who have only just begun to escape from a life of sin.

These teachers promise freedom from rules, but they are slaves to their own lusts. Whatever defeats a person makes him its slave, like a captive taken in war. True freedom in Christ is different. It sets us free from sin's rule so we can gladly obey God.

Some people turned away from the world's filth through knowing Jesus Christ. But if they get tangled up in it again, like an animal caught in a net, and sin beats them, they end up worse off than before. They have now sinned against more light.

differ.view: People can clean up their outward lives through knowing about Christ without ever being truly changed inside. So this verse does not mean true Christians fall away.
These people had truly escaped sin through faith in Christ, so a real believer can turn back and be lost.

notes.meaning: It would have been better never to know the way of righteousness than to know it and then turn away from God's holy command. Knowing more and still turning away brings heavier guilt. It is like a servant who knows his master's will and ignores it on purpose.

Peter quotes two sayings. One is about a dog going back to its vomit, from Proverbs 26:11. The other is about a washed pig going back to roll in the mud. Such people have returned to the filth they once seemed to leave. The blame is theirs, not the gospel's. Yet even this is not hopeless: anyone who grieves over turning back can still believe in Jesus and be saved.

differ.view: The dog stayed a dog and the pig stayed a pig. These people never had a real change of heart. True believers still sin, but they do not fall away from God's grace.
These people had truly repented and been washed, which shows that a real believer can fall from grace.
